note: The town on the BARE plate (1536x1024) — the aerial establishing view, for
MainMenu, the Town hub and AdventureBoard.
THIS SCENE HAS NO FIGURES, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. The plate is an aerial: a
house is ~90px tall, so a person is 10-14px. Every actor strip is 21-48px, and
scaling pixel art down by 0.3 with a nearest filter destroys it — the figures
would be both wrong-sized and mangled. Putting people here needs new art cut at
aerial scale, not the strips we have (audit M4B-ACT-04).
It has no lights either, and that is also deliberate: this is the one DAYTIME
plate. A warm lantern glow on a sunlit street reads as a rendering bug.
What the plate actually wants is in spec 09 §5: water shimmer on the harbour
(rank 4), cloud drift across the top (rank 7), the windmill sails on the right
ridge, the fountain in the square, and gulls. Every one of those needs either a
shader layer SceneStage does not have yet or art that does not exist yet, which
is audit M4B-VFX-01. So this file is honest about being a plate for now: the
screen gets the full-frame bare town instead of a mockup crop with baked label
pills, and the life arrives when the layer that can carry it does.
THE FIGURES ARE STILL ABSENT (see above), but the aerial is no longer inert: spec 09 §5
row 4's water shimmer runs on the sea, the harbour and the river mouth, and row 7's cloud
drift landed with W2-STAGE2 (next paragraph). Row 8 (the airship: 160x140px of sky patched
behind a cut airship) and the windmill sails stay in M4B-VFX-01 until W4-LIFE.
W2-STAGE2 (STAGE-14, PIPE-10, TOWN-12): the sky drifts and the chimneys smoke. `scroll`
slides W1-VFX's two periodic cloud strips (gen_clouds.py, the plate's own sky tones) over
rows 0-200 at 3 and 5 px/s, at 0.42 / 0.38 opacity (denser veiled the painted sky) — the strips
are 220 tall and fade out by row ~180; the quad crops their last sparse rows so nothing moves
below row 200 (the plan's "rows 0-200"; the review measured 73 px drifting in 200-223) and the peaks and the
castle stay clear; `smoke` emitters sit on three chimney stacks measured at 3x on the
plate: the hall's left roof (814,362), the east house (990,516), the west house's ridge
(402,350). Both hold under reduced_motion (the plume is preprocessed, so a held stage
still shows one) and go under reduced_effects. The airship and the sails stay owed.
W4-LIFE (STAGE-14): the sails turn and the gulls cross. `rotor` spins the two windmills'
sails — cut from this plate's own pixels by tools/art/patch_plate.py (sail_a hub (1337,328),
sail_b hub (1291,434); the plate under them is patched by the same recorded step) — about
their axles at 0.18 / -0.14 rad/s (one turn in ~35-45 s; the two turn opposite ways, as
two mills in one wind never quite agree). `flyers` sends three gulls (gull.png, 12x6x3)
round closed splines: two circling the harbour mouth at the bottom right, one crossing
the sky band under the peaks. Both layers hold under reduced_motion (the sails at
their painted angle, so that frame IS the painting) and stay under reduced_effects.
The airship stays owed.
